doc.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

chapter: Woody Herman, Buddy Rich and Thad Jones
title: Buddy Rich's band
summary: He only worked with Buddy when he needed a baritone player; Buddy's lectures were too strict, though he had good bands.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well you sat in a number of good big band sections.

I didn’t work with Buddy all the time. I only seemed to work with Buddy when he was looking for a baritone player. But I would never do that, I would never go out with Buddy’s band. Buddy was too strict for me. I couldn’t deal with that.
He was a task master, to put it nicely.

Yeah. Well I mean we used to play a set and then he’d get everybody in the band room and tell everybody how rotten they all were and how they couldn’t play. And you had to deal with all these lectures all the time.
He really built up the morale, huh?
But he had some good bands.
Yeah he had some good bands.
